newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary BUX record run slows down in hectic trade.
newsitem.headline: Hungary BUX record run slows down in hectic trade.

text.p: The record breaking bull run on the Budapest bourse continued at a much slower pace on Wednesday as profit-taking and position closings on the futures market have eaten up most of the market's early gains.
"The market turned crazy by the end of the session," one trader said. "There were some sales, mainly in (oil company) MOL, which could be linked to position closings."
The BUX index, which in early trade ran to a new trading high of 6,323.19 points, finished at 6,257.05 points, a new closing high, up 4.14 points.

"Recent warnings of sellings within two weeks of June BUX expiry (on June 16) are about to become a reality," the trader said. "They predicted that there would be position closings, the sale of shares,...at whatever price."
The last deal in June BUX futures was made at 6,260 points, 10 points below Tuesday's settlement price.
MOL which advanced to 3,680 forints, plunged back to end at 3,550, down 95 forints or 2.61 percent.

Another trader said that the market's recent bull run which saw the BUX index firming more than five percent in three sessions to Wednesday, triggered profit-takings. But he added he did not expect a turnaround in the market's fortunes.

"This was a day of mixed feelings," the other trader said. "A profit-taking came in late trading but this was not surprising after a rather strong Monday and Tuesday," he said. "But I don't expect the trend to turn around," he added.

On Wednesday several stocks powered ahead to new record levels. Among them were plastics products group Pannonplast which soared to 9,680 forints before retreating to close at 9,575, up 424 and pharmaceuticals Richter which rallied to 16,150, before closing at 15,750, down 50.
Analysts said corrections were imminent but in a somewhat longer term the bourse's outlook was encouraging as fresh money reaches the market.

"Investors still think they can find real value (on the market) and one can agree with this opinion," said Rudi Voros, analyst at ICE Securities in London. "Of course, a technical correction has to come sooner or later, I would be very surprised it there weren't a correction this week."
But the analyst added that new foreign investors start to be appear on the Hungarian market.
"Companies produce good results, profit growth is quicker in (Hungary) than in the Czech Republic or Poland," Voros said. "Many investors already look at the 1998 forecasts and invest accordingly."

Elsewhere on the market on Wednesday, machinery company Mezogep gained almost eight percent or 180 forints to end at 2,480 after it said it almost doubled its operating profits in the first quarter over last year's Q1, although its net profit fell due to one-off exchange rate losses.
